content.body:
The E-4 model is fast and has the heaviest armament of the 109's until the later G models. Possibly the best instantaneous turner of the 109's, this plane is as at home in a turn fight as it is in a fast, diving attack. The dedicated Bf109 pilot must its speed and climb rate to survive an encounter with bad odds. Combine its overall good performance with a cool-headed and confident pilot and the E can hold its own against any fighter, although late war era fighters will give it a very hard time. Against the RAF you must resist the temptation to turn flight exclusively, as both the Spitfire and Hurricane can about turn the 109 if pressed to the point of a pure turning duel.
However, climbing turns are a different story completely and can neutralize an enemy's turning advantage quickly in the 109's favor.
The E-4 has already begun to trade pure turning performance for firepower and speed (compared to its predecessor the E-1) ... a pattern that was to continue throughout the war.
